summary.headline: Vedanta Aluminium Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR21,105 crore (+45% YoY) and EBITDA INR10,499 crore (+134% YoY), with hot metal cost at USD1,698/t.
summary.overview: This was a combined joint call for five demerged Vedanta entities, with Vedanta Aluminium Metal (VAML) reporting its first quarter post demerger. VAML posted record aluminium production of 632 kt and record revenue and EBITDA, with EBITDA per ton rising from USD1,511 to USD1,804 quarter on quarter. Net debt to EBITDA fell from 1.3x to 0.9x and an interim dividend of INR8 per share was declared. Vedanta Limited (demerged parent) reported EBITDA of INR8,469 crore (57% margin) and PAT of INR5,294 crore on a continuing-operations basis, while Vedanta Power's Sakti Unit 1 outage weighed on its quarter.

financial_highlights.value: INR945 crore, incl. INR1,097 crore discontinued ops gain; continuing PAT -INR151 crore

segments.name: Vedanta Aluminium (VAML)
segments.commentary: Record aluminium output of 632 kt (+5% YoY, +3% QoQ) and alumina of 826 kt (+41% YoY, -6% QoQ); sales 615 kt; value-added products record 389 kt (+14% YoY).

segments.name: Vedanta Oil & Gas
segments.commentary: Gross operated production 77.7 kboe/d (Rajasthan 63.1, offshore 11.6, OALP 3.1); unit opex USD17.4/bbl, down 3% QoQ; Brent up about 15% QoQ supported EBITDA.

segments.name: Vedanta Power
segments.commentary: Sales 5,224 million units (+38% YoY); Meenakshi record quarterly EBITDA INR112 crore; Talwandi Sabo availability 86% from 77% QoQ; Sakti Unit 1 restart targeted end Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Vedanta Iron & Steel
segments.commentary: Steel sellable production 582 kt at 12% EBITDA margin; iron ore output 2.6 Mt (+4% YoY); overall margin 14% vs 11% last year.

segments.name: Vedanta Limited (Zinc, Copper, FACOR)
segments.commentary: Zinc India refined metal 260 kt (+4% YoY) at lowest-ever cost of USD851/t; Gamsberg cost USD1,549/t; FACOR best-ever quarterly EBITDA INR101 crore; Copper India sales 53 kt (+3% YoY).

guidance_outlook: VAML full-year hot metal cost guidance unchanged at USD1,650-1,700/t; Q2 may be marginally higher due to monsoon power plant shutdowns.
VAML FY27 alumina output of 4.0-4.1 Mt from Lanjigarh, with H2 weighted volumes expected.
VAML FY27 capex about INR5,000 crore (INR2,000-2,500 crore BALCO); FY28 capex about INR3,500-4,000 crore; net debt about INR29,500 crore.
Vedanta India consol EBITDA outlook about USD9.5-10 billion (per management); Vedanta Power Sakti Unit 2 completion targeted by end of FY27.

Vedanta Limited FY27 growth capex about INR7,000 crore and maintenance capex about INR4,000 crore; Vedanta Resources repayment and refinancing plans include about USD1 billion bridge financing in FY28.
capex_capacity: VAML: Sijimali bauxite mine awaiting consent to operate, mining targeted after monsoon, with 1-2 Mt this year and 6-7 Mt next year; Kuraloi coal mine to produce about 2 Mt this year and 8 Mt next year.
BALCO Potline expansion: 24 kt produced in Q1 vs 22 kt plan; full capacity exit this year; about 260-270 kt this year and 435 kt total run-rate after next year.
Vedanta Power: 4.2 GW operating, targeting 4.8 GW by end FY27; further 7.2 GW planned from FY30; Sakti Unit 1 restart targeted end Q2 FY27 and Unit 2 completion by end FY27.
Vedanta Iron & Steel: Bokaro expansion Stage 1 forest clearance received, Stage 2 expected by end Q2, project completion by end FY27; Goa ductile iron pipe project later this year.
Zinc International Gamsberg Phase 2 (200 ktpa) likely to commence in August; Zinc India smelter expansion (250 ktpa) by Q2 FY29; Copper India capacity 222 ktpa, to 229 ktpa after debottlenecking.
demand_pricing: Global aluminium prices remained buoyant on supply-side constraints; VAML alumina cost about USD780/t in Q1, guided toward about USD750/t in Q2.
VAML hedged 28% of volumes for balance of FY27 at average USD3,062/t; Q1 hedge 293 kt at USD2,813/t; Q2 hedge 270 kt at USD2,830/t.

Vedanta Power: import coal prices up over 60% but coal cost contained 12% YoY by shifting to Indian coal (65-70% of consumption); about 74% of volume under medium/long-term PPAs; Kerala 1-year PPA at INR5.96-5.97/unit.
Copper International rod sales down 51% YoY due to Middle East supply chain disruption.
Oil & Gas: sales cyclical, about 85% of volumes sold in Q1 per management, with remainder liquidating post-monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why does VAML's segment EBITDA sum to about INR10,527 crore vs reported INR10,499 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is a consolidation adjustment for intercompany transactions between BALCO and VAML.

qa_highlights.question: Can VAML achieve 4.0-4.1 Mt alumina for FY27 given recent run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects higher H2 volumes since monsoon months are weaker for power and alumina; the 4.0-4.1 Mt target is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend capacity across the five entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a 4-5% dividend yield on each company's market cap as the group target; VAML (about INR18-20k crore of INR35k crore combined market cap) may provide about half of dividends. Policy is now descriptive, decided by each board.

qa_highlights.question: VAML leverage comfort and expansion timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR29,500 crore; leverage below 1x comfortable for a 3 Mtpa expansion, which remains on the drawing board with a board update expected in about a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Sijimali bauxite timeline and savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Consent to operate expected this quarter; mining after monsoon via MDO partner. Captive alumina is about USD50-60/t cheaper than bought-out, with a further USD40-50/t saving once Sijimali ramps up.

qa_highlights.question: Vedanta Power Sakti restart timeline and PPA tie-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 1 restart targeted end Sept or early Oct; 26% revival complete; no hurdles seen. About 600 MW tied up of the 1,600 MW Meenakshi and Athena capacity; management is selective on PPA pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Vedanta Resources debt outflows?
qa_highlights.answer: About USD400 million needed for the rest of FY27 (mainly interest and KCM funding), largely met via dividends; FY28 about USD1 billion including bridge; FY29 about USD730 million; brand fee fixed at 3% until March 2029.

risks_watch: Sakti Unit 1 restart slipped to end-Sept/early-Oct and Unit 2 completion targeted by end FY27; insurance claim assessment for Unit 1 still pending, and only about 600 MW of the 1,600 MW Meenakshi and Athena capacity is tied up under PPAs.

Sijimali bauxite mine start depends on consent to operate expected this quarter; mining only after monsoon, with 1-2 Mt this year against 6-7 Mt next year. Q2 VAML hot metal cost guided marginally higher due to monsoon power plant shutdowns.
VAML alumina output of 4.0-4.1 Mt for FY27 needs a sharply higher H2 after Q1 alumina of 826 kt and a 6% QoQ decline; hedge book covers only 28% of balance-FY27 volumes at about USD3,062/t.
Zinc International volume and cost: management says some FY27 volume shortfall is likely, with a cost revision possible only in H2; Gamsberg Phase 2 (200 ktpa) start targeted for August.

Vedanta Resources refinancing: about USD400 million needed for the rest of FY27, about USD1 billion in FY28 including bridge financing, and dividend flows from group companies to cover it. Dividend policy is now descriptive, so payouts are at each board's discretion.

Oil & Gas: Q1 gains rode on Brent up about 15% QoQ while production declined; continuing PAT was negative INR151 crore after a INR345 crore net exceptional charge, with reported PAT lifted by the INR1,097 crore discontinued-ops gain.
key_quotes: We are confident that our EBITDA run rate will remain resilient across commodity cycles, driven by higher volumes from BALCO expansion, increased value-added product and domestic market penetration and continued cost reductions through backward integration.
Our guidance on the cost for full year remains unchanged at USD1,650 to USD1,700 per ton.
Now coming to the new expansion 3 MTPA, presently, we explained last time also, as of now, we are on a drawing board.
Ritesh, you are aware that this matter is sub judice, that is where I did not want to indicate the number because you are aware that we are getting this under the court order as of now.
summary.management_tone: Confident on VAML and group cash generation, with firm guidance on hot metal cost, BALCO ramp-up and the leverage path. Cautious and less specific on timelines for Sijimali, Sakti restart and the next 3 Mtpa expansion, where management repeatedly said approvals or board decisions are pending. Several answers on the bauxite OMC procurement, Oil & Gas quarter-on-quarter sales and the real estate unlock were deferred or kept high level.

adds.what: BALCO potline expansion, 24 kt produced in Q1 vs 22 kt plan; ~260-270 kt this year, 435 kt total run-rate after next year
Vedanta Power capacity from 4.2 GW to 4.8 GW by end FY27

Sakti Unit 2 completion by end FY27

growth.why: Management held FY27 hot metal cost guidance at USD1,650-1,700/t and Lanjigarh alumina at 4.0-4.1 Mt, with BALCO potline volume of 260-270 kt this year and Vedanta Power/Iron & Steel capacity adds due by end FY27; no explicit consolidated revenue growth guide was given, and Q1 revenue grew 45% YoY, though much of this is price-driven and backed by partial, not contracted, capacity evidence.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Hot metal cost guided at USD1,650-1,700/t for FY27 vs Q1 USD1,698/t, and EBITDA per ton rose to USD1,804/t from USD1,511/t QoQ, though Q2 cost may be marginally higher on monsoon power shutdowns and alumina hedges cover only 28% of balance-FY27 volumes at USD3,062/t.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: BALCO potline reaching full capacity exit this year (24 kt in Q1 vs 22 kt plan, 260-270 kt this year, 435 kt run-rate after next year), Vedanta Power 4.2 GW to 4.8 GW by end FY27, and Bokaro Stage 2 by end Q2 with completion by end FY27; Sakti Unit 1 restart end Q2 FY27 is firmly targeted, though it has already slipped to end-Sept/early-Oct.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Lanjigarh alumina guided to 4.0-4.1 Mt for FY27 vs Q1 826 kt (about 3.3 Mt annualised), requiring a sharply higher H2; aluminium at 632 kt in Q1 (+5% YoY) and Sijimali bauxite 6-7 Mt next year support volume ramp, with Q2 monsoon weakness a near-term drag.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: VAML FY27 capex about INR5,000 crore and net debt about INR29,500 crore with leverage at 0.9x, and a 3 Mtpa expansion is on the drawing board with a board update expected in about a quarter, but approvals are still pending.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 hot metal cost and alumina guidance unchanged, and flagged a marginally higher Q2 cost from monsoon power shutdowns, so there is no sign of a raise despite record Q1 EBITDA of INR10,499 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Alumina needs 4.0-4.1 Mt but Q1 was 826 kt, Sijimali bauxite mining starts only after monsoon (1-2 Mt this year), Zinc International flagged likely FY27 volume shortfall, and Sakti Unit 1 restart has already slipped to end-Sept/early-Oct.

rows.label: Sijimali bauxite captive mining saving
rows.why: Captive alumina is USD50-60/t cheaper than bought-out, with a further USD40-50/t saving once Sijimali ramps up from 1-2 Mt this year to 6-7 Mt next year, though consent to operate is still pending.

rows.label: VAML net debt to EBITDA below 1x
rows.why: Net debt to EBITDA already fell from 1.3x to 0.9x QoQ with net debt about INR29,500 crore, and management says leverage below 1x is comfortable even for a 3 Mtpa expansion.

rows.label: Vedanta Power Sakti Unit 1 restart and PPA tie-ups
rows.why: Unit 1 26% revival complete with no hurdles seen, but insurance claim is pending and only about 600 MW of the 1,600 MW Meenakshi and Athena capacity is tied up under PPAs.

tone.note: Management was confident on record VAML output, the INR8 interim dividend, leverage at 0.9x and the hot metal cost guide, but cautious and vague on Sijimali consent, Sakti restart timing and the 3 Mtpa expansion approval; analysts pressed on the alumina 4.0-4.1 Mt H2 ramp and dividend capacity.
